claims.text: Annealing HfNbTaTiZr at 1100°C for 24–48 hours enhances chemical short-range order.
Enhanced chemical short-range order induces localized lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
The localized lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Enhanced chemical ordering modifies the harmonicity of lattice vibrations.
The ordering-related changes in lattice vibrations lower the elevated-temperature elastic modulus.
The ordering-related changes in lattice vibrations increase thermal expansion at elevated temperatures.
Relative to as-synthesized HfNbTaTiZr, annealed HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower elastic modulus between 600°C and 1000°C.
Relative to as-synthesized HfNbTaTiZr, annealed HfNbTaTiZr will have a higher thermal expansion coefficient between 600°C and 1000°C.
The elastic or thermal response curves will contain an observable inflection indicating the onset of the proposed effects.
The proposed relationships are expected to hold from 600°C to 1000°C when grain growth and secondary-phase formation are negligible.
Grain growth or secondary-phase formation during annealing could confound attribution of mechanical and thermal changes to chemical short-range order.
